question: to the Commission Tomáš Zdechovský (PPE), Alexandr Vondra (ECR), Sebastian Tynkkynen (ECR), Anna Zalewska (ECR), Diana Iovanovici Şoşoacă (NI), Zala Tomašič (PPE), Merja Kyllönen (The Left), Stefan Köhler (PPE), Ondřej Krutílek (ECR), Jaroslav Bžoch (PfE), Jana Nagyová (PfE), Ondřej Knotek (PfE), Tomáš Kubín (PfE), Mircea-Gheorghe Hava (PPE), Miriam Lexmann (PPE), Kateřina Konečná (NI), Massimiliano Salini (PPE), Jan Farský (PPE) Subject:

Annex V (Row 1) to the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation1 (PPWR) restricts certain grouped packaging formats while allowing exceptions where packaging is ‘necessary for handling’. However, this concept is not defined, and under the regulation the Commission is not required to provide further clarification before early 2027. This creates immediate legal uncertainty for operators who have to adapt packaging formats ahead of the 2030 deadline. Without clear interpretation, companies cannot determine whether widely used solutions, such as plastic shrink wrap, will remain permitted. In addition, a premature shift away from certain grouped packaging formats may lead to increased use of alternative packaging, potentially resulting in higher packaging volumes and waste, contrary to the environmental objectives of the PPWR. 1.
How does the Commission interpret ‘necessary for handling’ under Annex V (Row 1) to the PPWR?
Given that clarification may only be provided by early 2027, how will the Commission ensure that operators can prepare in time to meet the 2030 requirements?
How will the Commission ensure that implementation of Annex V avoids unintended environmental impacts, including increased packaging waste?

Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC (OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/40/oj).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.7.2026) The Commission fully shares the objective of adopting the guidelines without undue delay and is actively working towards their timely adoption. To support this process, an external contractor has been appointed to assist the Commission with the preparatory work. This preparatory work includes, among others, the development of illustrative examples and further clarification of key concepts, such as ‘necessary to facilitate handling’. The Commission intends to discuss the progress and preliminary outcomes of this work already during 2026, in close dialogue with Member States and stakeholders. This approach aims to provide legal certainty, clarity and predictability for industry and national authorities, while supporting a practical and harmonised implementation of the Regulation across the EU. Annex V focuses on phasing out unnecessary packaging, and the impact assessment accompanying the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation1 concluded that it contributes significantly to reducing packaging waste overall. The Commission is committed to develop high-quality guidelines to ensure avoidance of unintended increases in packaging waste and has mobilised the necessary technical support to this end. For instance, the involvement of the European Food Safety Authority in developing exemptions from the restriction on the use of single-use plastic packaging for fresh fruit and vegetables weighing less than 1.5 kg ensures a robust scientific basis.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging
and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025.
